This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, praying to modify the judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.595/2018 dated 20-01-2020 by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM and MACT,
Chikkamagaluru and enhance the compensation of `10,00,000/- with 9% interest per annum in the interest of justice and equity and grant such other reliefs as this court deems fit in the circumstances of the case in the interest of justice and equity.

This Miscellaneous First Appeal coming on for Admission through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing, this day, the Court delivered the following:
 -3-  MFA No. 1992 of 2021  JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Chief Judicial Magistrate and Motor Vehicles Accident Claims Tribunal, Chikkamagaluru,
(hereinafter for brevity referred to as "the Tribunal"), in its judgment and award dated 20-01-2020,
in M.V.C.No.595/2018.
2.

sentences.text: The summary of the case of the claimant before the Tribunal was that, on the date 27-09-2018,
he , joined by one of his friends was proceeding on a Motor Cycle bearing registration Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
2 No.KA-18/U-1561 from Chikkamagaluru to Kuduvalli village.

When they were near Bola Rameshwara Temple on K.M. Road, Chikkamagaluru, at about 8:00 p.m., the respondent No.1 being the driver of a motor vehicle Bus bearing registration No.KA-18/A-8371, drove the said Bus in a rash and negligent manner, with high speed and dashed against the Motor cycle of the claimant from behind.
Due to the said road traffic accident, the petitioner/claimant fell down and sustained multiple grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to M.G. Hospital, Chikkamagaluru, where he was treated as an in-patient from the date 27-09-2018 to the date 29-09-2018.
Thereafter, he was shifted to the Wenlock Hospital, Mangaluru, where he was treated as an in-patient from the date 30-09-2018 to the date 27-10-2018.
The claimant has stated that, he had spent more than a sum of `1,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

He also stated that, prior to the road traffic accident, he was doing Shade loping work and was earning a sum of `15,000/- per month, however, after the road traffic accident, he is not in a position to do any work due to the injuries suffered by him.

With this, he has claimed a compensation of a sum of `5,00,000/- from the respondents No.1, 2 and 3 before the Tribunal,
holding them respectively as the driver, owner and insurer of the Bus.
3. In response to the notice served upon them before the Tribunal, the respondent Nos.1 to 3 appeared through their counsels.

The respondents No.1 and 2 have filed their Statement of objections wherein they have denied the manner of the occurrence of the road traffic accident, as claimed by the claimant in his claim petition.
They contended that the petitioner/claimant had no valid Driving Licence to ride the Motor Cycle as at the time of the said road traffic accident.
The respondent No.3 - Insurance Company denied its liability towards the claimant.
4. Before the Tribunal, the claimant got himself examined as PW-1 and got marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-13.

On behalf of the respondents, no witness was examined, however, two documents in the form of a copy of the Driving Licence and a copy of the Insurance Policy were got marked as Exs.R-1 and R-2 respectively.

5. After analysing the evidence and the materials placed before it, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation under the following heads with the sum shown against them:

 No.
 1 Disability at 20% 3,12,000-00
2 Pain and sufferings 75,000-00
3 Medical expenses and hospital 10,000-00  charges

4 Loss of income during laid up 60,000-00  period Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
3  5
Food and nourishment 12,000-00

8 Loss of amenities 11,000-00

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `5,00,000/- with interest at the rate of `9% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation of the entire amount, holding the owner and Insurer jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation and directed the Insurer to deposit the award amount.

It is against the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
7.
The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) and the learned counsel for respondent No.1 (insurer) before this Court are physically appearing before the Court.

On a memo filed by the learned counsel for the appellant, notice to Respondent No.2 (driver of the offending vehicle) and respondent No.3 (owner of the offending vehicle) is dispensed with vide order dated 14-06-2022.
8. Though this appeal is listed at the stage of admission, however, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the same is taken up for its final disposal.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that, he has the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits, as such, summoning of the Trial Court records is also not required and that he would place those copies before the Court.
With this, he places the copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits for a perusal and their return to him.
10. In the light of the above, heard the arguments from both side.

Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the certified copies of the pleadings, depositions and exhibits placed before the Court by the learned counsel for the appellant.

11. The present appeal being the claimant's appeal and the respondent Insurer having not preferred either cross-objection or a counter appeal, the question of occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged by the claimant and also the alleged rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle is not in dispute.

Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
4
Further, the claimant, who got himself examined as PW-1, reiterated the contentions taken up by him in his claim petition even in his examination-in-chief also.

In support of his contention, he got produced and marked documents from Exs.P-1 to P-13, which inter alia includes Police notice,
copies of the FIR, complaint, scene of offence panchanama, wound certificate, medical bills and discharge summary, which goes to establish the occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date,
time and place as mentioned in the claim petition and the claimant sustaining injuries in the said accident, so also the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the alleged offending Motor vehicle Bus bearing registration No.KA-18/A-8371 in causing the said road traffic accident which has inflicted injuries upon the claimant.
Thus, the only question that remains for consideration is, whether the claimant is entitled for any - 10 - enhancement in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in the matter.

12. The learned counsel for the appellant (claimant) in his argument submitted that, though the clamant did not produce any documents to establish his income at a sum of `15,000/- per month,
however, the Tribunal should have taken the notional income of the claimant at a sum of `12,500/-
per month, which was the prevailing notional income for the relevant year of the occurrence of the year of accident.
However, the Tribunal has taken a sum of `10,000/- per month as the notional income of the claimant, as such, the same requires to be enhanced by this Court.
He further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of amenities is also on the lower side and requires to be enhanced.

13. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 - Insurance Company, in his brief argument submitted that, the quantum of compensation - 11 - awarded by the Tribunal being just, fair and reasonable, does not warrant any interference at the hands of this Court.

He further submitted that, the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal which is at `9% per annum on the compensation amount is on the higher side and as such, the same requires to be reduced to `6% per annum.
14.
The claimant has stated that, in the accident, he suffered multiple grievous injuries, major one being a crush injury to the right palm.
In his support, he has produced a copy of the wound certificate marked at Ex.P-5.

The same would go to show that, the Doctor, after examining the injured, has opined that, the claimant had sustained de-gloving injury to the right hand, which he has considered as a crush injury of 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th finger with functional limitation.
An abrasion injury over the left hand thumb and left leg measuring 1 cm. x 1 cm. was also noticed.
The Doctor has opined that the de-gloving injury was grievous in nature and abrasion injury was simple in nature.

The claimant has also produced photographs Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
5 - 12 - showing his injuries and also has produced discharge summary at Ex.P-9.

It is considering the wound certificate, discharge summary and the photographs of the injuries, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `75,000/- towards pain and sufferings, which I consider as just, fair and reasonable compensation, warranting no interference at the hands of this Court.
15.

Even though the claimant has contended that, he has spent a sum of `1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, however, admittedly, he has not produced and marked the required medical prescriptions and bills to corroborate his said contention.
Considering the available material, the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `10,000/- under the head of medical expenses and hospital charges.

After going through the discharge summary at Ex.P-9, considering the nature of injuries and looking at the photographs of the injuries filed by the claimant, I am of the view that the said medical expenses and hospital charges deserves an enhancement by a sum - 13 - of another `10,000/-, thus making it to a total of a sum of `20,000/- under the said head.
16. Towards the heads of 'food and nourishment', 'conveyance' and 'attendant charges', the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of a sum of `12,000/-, `10,000/- and `10,000/- respectively.

Considering the duration of treatment undergone by the claimant in the Hospital as an in-patient,
nature of injuries sustained and the circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the said compensation awarded under those heads is just, fair and reasonable and warrants no interference at the hands of this Court.
17. The claimant, in his evidence as PW-1, has stated that at the time of the road traffic accident, he was working as a labourer and earning a sum of `15,000/- per month.
Admittedly, he has not produced any documents to prove his alleged income.
Therefore, rightly the Tribunal has decided to take the notional income, however, in the said process, it has taken the notional income of the - 14 - claimant at the rate of `10,000/- per month.

Since the road traffic accident has occurred in the year 2018, for which a large number of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunals in the State are taking notional income at the rate of `12,500/- per month, even in the case on hand also, the income of the claimant was required to be taken at a sum of `12,500/- per month.

If the said monthly income at `12,500/- is taken into consideration, the loss of income during laid up period, which, according to the Tribunal, is a period of six months, would be short by a sum of `15,000/- [i.e. `12,500 x 6 months = `75,000/- (-) `10,000/-x6 months = `60,000/- = `15,000/-].
Thus, under the head of 'loss of income during the laid up period', the claimant is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `15,000/- as enhancement.

Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
6 18.
The claimant has stated in his evidence as PW-1 that, at the time of the road traffic accident, he was aged about 48 years.

However, the Driving Licence produced by him at Ex.P-13, wherein his date of birth is shown to be - 15 - 01-07-1969, which goes to show that, as on the date of the occurrence of the road traffic accident, he was 49 years of age.
Thus, the standard multiplier applicable for the said age is '13'.
The claimant has stated that due to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident, he has suffered some disability and that he could not even hold a glass of tea in his right hand.
It is after going through the discharge summary and the wound certificate, the Tribunal has assessed the percentage of disability at 20% to the whole body.
Since the said fixation/assessment of the disability is not disputed from the respondent's side, I retain the same.
Thus, towards loss of future income/disability, the quantum of compensation would come to `12,500/-x 12 monthsx'13'x20/100= `3,90,000/-.
After deducting a sum of `3,12,000/-, awarded by the Tribunal under this head, the claimant is entitled for the differential amount of a sum of `78,000/- as enhancement.

Noticing the fact that the claimant has suffered loss of amenities and comforts in life, on account of the nature of the injures and also the percentage of disability, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `11,000/- as compensation.

However, considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the fact that he has suffered disability to the right hand palm, I am of the view that, the quantum of compensation under the head of loss of amenities and comforts in life requires to be enhanced to bring it to a total sum of `20,000/-.
20.

Though the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 - Insurance Company contended that the rate of interest awarded on the compensation amount, which is at `9% per annum is on the higher side and requires to be reduced, but the fact remains that challenging the quantification or the rate of interest, the respondent No.1 - Insurance Company has not preferred any appeal or cross objection.

Considering the circumstance of the case, occurrence of the year of the road traffic accident and the - 17 - total quantum of compensation awarded, I do not want to modify the rate of interest ordered by the Tribunal.
21. Barring the above, the claimant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for any modification or enhancement of compensation under any other existing heads.

Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
7 22.
Thus, as analysed above, the claimant is entitled for a modified compensation as tabulated below:

 No.
 1 Disability at 20% 3,90,000-00
2 Pain
and sufferings
3 Medical expenses and hospital 20,000-00  charges  4 Loss of income during laid up 75,000-00  period  5 Food and nourishment 12,000-00
6 Conveyance charges 10,000-00
7 Attendant charges 10,000-00  8 Loss of amenities 20,000-00  Total 6,12,000-00  - 18

- Since the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal at a sum of `5,00,000/-
is in short by a sum of `1,12,000/-, for the said enhancement of a sum of `1,12,000/-
only, the impugned judgment and award deserves to be interfered with.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER [i] The appeal filed by the claimant stands allowed in part;
[ii] The impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Chief Judicial Magistrate and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Chikkamagaluru, dated 20-01-2020, in M.V.C.No.595/2018, is hereby modified to the extent that the compensation awarded at `5,00,000/- is enhanced by a sum of `1,12,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Twelve Thousand only), thus fixing the total compensation at Mallesh vs The Branch Manager on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2642955/
8 - 19 - `6,12,000/- (Rupees Six Lakh Twelve Thousand only).
[iii] The rest of the order of the Tribunal with respect to fixing the liability upon the respondents and directing the respondent No.1 herein - Insurance Company to deposit the awarded amount, rate of interest awarded, terms regarding release of the amount awarded shall all remain unaltered.
Draw the modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal, without delay.
Sd/-
